lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 20: RBAC and ServiceAccounts
lesson.description: Give a Pod its own identity, grant it exactly the API access it needs with Roles and bindings, and check every permission with kubectl auth can-i.
lesson.tested: Roles, bindings, can-i, Pod tokens and API calls tested on kind v0.33.0, node v1.37.0, 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Nothing is allowed until a binding says so. Give each workload its own ServiceAccount, grant the smallest Role that works, and prove it with kubectl auth can-i before you ship.

cheatsheet.intro: Identity, permissions, and the commands from Lesson 20.

rows.name: Authentication then RBAC
rows.role: Each API request is authenticated (who) and then authorized (may they). Permissions only add up; there are no deny rules.

rows.name: Role vs ClusterRole
rows.role: Roles and ClusterRoles hold rules. RoleBindings grant them in one namespace. ClusterRoleBindings grant them everywhere. A ClusterRole plus a RoleBinding reuses view, edit and admin per namespace.

rows.name: ServiceAccount
rows.role: A Pod's identity. Its token is mounted by the kubelet, bound to the Pod, and rotated. Turn it off with automountServiceAccountToken: false when the app does not call the API.

items.what: kubectl auth whoami shows the subject. Add --as to ask about a ServiceAccount.
A Role for deployments with apiGroups empty answered no. apps/v1 means the group is apps. After that change, can-i answered yes.
A binding with --serviceaccount=default:helper grants helper in default, not in k8s-from-zero. get rolebinding -o wide shows default/helper.
Permissions only add up. There are no deny rules.

commands.cmd: kubectl auth can-i list pods -n k8s-from-zero --as=system:serviceaccount:k8s-from-zero:inspector

homework.intro: Use the kind cluster and the namespace k8s-from-zero. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: Where do RoleBindings and ClusterRoleBindings apply, and how do you reuse view in one namespace?
exercises.a: RoleBindings grant a Role or ClusterRole in one namespace. ClusterRoleBindings grant a ClusterRole everywhere. A ClusterRole plus a RoleBinding is how you reuse view, edit and admin per namespace.

exercises.q: What is a ServiceAccount, and how do you stop the kubelet mounting a token?
exercises.a: A ServiceAccount is a Pod's identity. The kubelet mounts a token, bound to the Pod and rotated. Set automountServiceAccountToken: false when the app does not call the API.

exercises.q: Are there deny rules in RBAC?
exercises.a: No. Permissions only add up. Nothing is allowed until a binding says so.

exercises.q: Before any Role is bound, what does kubectl auth can-i say for the inspector ServiceAccount listing pods? After you apply the pod-reader Role and binding?
exercises.a: Before the binding, can-i is no, and an API call from the Pod gets 403. After the Role and RoleBinding, can-i list/get pods in that namespace is yes. can-i delete pods should still be no if the Role only grants get, watch and list.

exercises.q: How does the lesson tell you to read a 403, and how do you reproduce it?
exercises.a: Read a 403 as who, what, which, where, then reproduce it with kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<name>.

exercises.q: What is the difference between kubectl create token and the token already mounted in the Pod?
exercises.a: create token issues a TokenRequest with the duration you pass (the lab used 10m). The mounted token is bound to the Pod and rotated; the lesson took the default rotation timing from the docs and did not wait for a rotation.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: You bind a ClusterRole that can get nodes with a RoleBinding in one namespace. Can the ServiceAccount get nodes?
exercises.a: Nodes are cluster-scoped. A RoleBinding only grants namespaced use of a ClusterRole in that namespace, so cluster-scoped resources such as nodes need a ClusterRoleBinding. The lesson's node-reader step uses the binding that matches that scope.

exercises.q: A Pod has automountServiceAccountToken: false. Can it still call the API with the default mount?
exercises.a: No. The kubelet will not mount a token. The app has no default ServiceAccount credentials in the Pod.
